clue.text: This writer, inspired by that virtually small river

indicators.note: virtually means almost all, so the word that loses its final letter
inspired by means breathed in by, so the writer's letters go inside the shortened word

parts.note: the setter referring to themself gives ME
S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: An author claims to have been inspired by some modest little stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inspired by' looks like the writer's muse but means the writer is breathed in; 'virtually' then drops the final letter, leaving all but one.
explanation.definitionFit: The Thames is the river that flows through London, an example of the general term.

clue.text: Unfriendly crowd that is gathering close to memorial

parts.note: a host is a great crowd

indicators.note: gathering means taking in, so i.e. holds the next letter

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

indicators.note: close to means the last letter of the word memorial

explanation.surface: A sullen crowd assembles near a war memorial.
explanation.definitionFit: Hostile describes antagonistic, unwelcoming behaviour, a synonym of unfriendly.

clue.text: City rising in national importance

indicators.note: rising says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A metropolis climbs in significance on the national stage.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft left 'in' as a link word; it is the signal that the letters lie within the words. In a down clue 'rising' reads NALIM upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Milan is a major city in northern Italy, an example of the general term.

clue.text: Son finding refusing starter brings temptation

parts.note: S is the usual genealogical abbreviation for son

indicators.note: refusing starter means the conclusion word drops its first letter

parts.note: a deduction is a conclusion or finding

explanation.surface: A boy turning down the first course leads to a craving.
explanation.definitionFit: Seduction is the act of enticing or luring someone, close in sense to temptation.

clue.text: Murder drama in theatre that's bad?

definitions.meaning: the phrase used for a suspected killing
read literally, a stage play that is foul, that is, rotten

explanation.surface: A murder-mystery production that critics have panned.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the phrase literally: a play that is foul.
explanation.definitionFit: Police reports use the idiom for criminal violence, especially a suspected killing.

clue.text: Fine rowing crew in good condition reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly says the phrase is heard spoken rather than written

parts.note: a four is a rowing crew, and fit means in good condition

explanation.surface: A rowing crew in top shape is doing fine, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: FOUR plus FIT, spoken, matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A forfeit is a penalty paid, as a fine is; both are nouns here.

clue.text: Disconcert group of persons on horseback?

definitions.meaning: jockeys mounted are said to be up, and a set is a group

explanation.surface: A mounted troop unsettles someone.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is whimsical: a set of riders who are all up.
explanation.definitionFit: To upset someone is to throw them off balance emotionally; the second sense splits the word.

clue.text: Benefit completely will stop, in distressing fashion

indicators.note: will stop means plugging a gap, so the second phrase goes into the first

parts.note: pay is a benefit, as in an advantage or reward
in full means completely

explanation.surface: Someone frets that a welfare benefit is going to end altogether.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb describes something done in a way that hurts or upsets, matching the phrase.

clue.text: Comparatively cross when earring gets broken

indicators.note: an earring that is broken is in pieces, so its letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone becomes more annoyed when a piece of jewellery snaps.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative of a word meaning annoyed, so more annoyed than another.

clue.text: Student extremely anxious over labelling for vinaigrette, perhaps

indicators.note: over signals that the student and the extremes of anxious are turned over and read backwards

parts.note: L is a learner, the student driver's plate

indicators.note: extremely means take only the extreme letters of the word anxious

parts.note: addressing a parcel is labelling it

explanation.surface: A nervous student frets about how to label a jar of vinaigrette.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns L plus AS round to SAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Vinaigrette is one example of the oil-based sauces poured over leaves.

clue.text: Top pastry contains ultimate in Himalayan salt, according to chemist

indicators.note: contains says the pastry dish holds the other pieces within it

parts.note: a pie is a pastry dish

indicators.note: ultimate in means the last letter of the word Himalayan

parts.note: NaCl is the chemical formula for common salt, sodium chloride

explanation.surface: A chef tops a pie with pink Himalayan salt on a chemist's advice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'salt, according to chemist' is sodium chloride written as its formula; 'contains' puts that and the last letter of Himalayan inside the pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinnacle is the highest point or summit, a synonym of top as a noun.

clue.text: Quarrel at home making lunch

parts.note: a tiff is a minor quarrel
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: A domestic row breaks out while a meal is being prepared.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiffin is an Anglo-Indian word for a light midday meal, still used in Britain and India.

clue.text: Stars seen in outwardly grotesque car

indicators.note: outwardly means only the outside letters of the word grotesque

parts.note: the Mini is a famous small British car

explanation.surface: Celebrities spotted climbing into a hideous car.
explanation.definitionFit: Gemini is a zodiac constellation, a group of stars known as the Twins.

clue.text: First gun Laura shot, preceded by indecision originally

indicators.note: preceded by says the initial comes before the rearranged words
originally means the first letter of the word indecision
shot suggests the letters are scattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: Laura hesitated before firing her first gun.
explanation.definitionFit: An inaugural event is the opening or first one in a series.

clue.text: Acrobats in glasses?

definitions.meaning: performers who do somersaults and tumbles

explanation.surface: Circus performers seen through spectacles, or performers inside drinking vessels.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: gymnasts who do somersaults, and straight-sided drinking vessels.

clue.text: Keeping quiet, explosive Egham individual that usually raises voice

indicators.note: keeping means holding in, so the outer pieces surround the quiet letter
explosive suggests the town name is blown apart and its letters rearranged

parts.note: one means a single individual
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Someone from Egham, normally loud, is keeping quiet for once.
explanation.walkthrough: Egham is a town in Surrey, England. 'explosive' rearranges it to MEGAH; 'Keeping' puts P between MEGA and H.
explanation.definitionFit: A megaphone is a cone-shaped device used to amplify a speaker's words.

clue.text: Real ale enthusiasts rejected imbibing good North American brandy

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step
rejected means the group's initials are sent back, read backwards

parts.note: CAMRA is the Campaign for Real Ale, a British beer lovers' group

explanation.surface: Beer fans turn their noses up at a fine American spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: The Campaign for Real Ale is a British beer-lovers' group known by its initials; 'rejected' turns them round and 'imbibing' takes in the other letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Armagnac is a grape spirit distilled in Gascony, a regional type of the general drink.

clue.text: Pickled herring to start followed by sponge

indicators.note: followed by says the next piece comes after the first

parts.note: roll is the command to start, as when filming or a press begins
to mop is to sponge up

explanation.surface: A menu of herring to begin with, then cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A rollmop is a fillet of herring rolled around onion and preserved in vinegar.

clue.text: Painter, unknown character meeting queen after church

indicators.note: after says the other pieces come behind the church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
in algebra x, y and z stand for unknowns
Anne was a queen of Great Britain

explanation.surface: An artist and a mysterious figure meet the monarch after a service.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Cézanne was a French Post-Impressionist artist.

clue.text: Overheard old man that regularly lets off steam?

indicators.note: overheard says the word is heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: a geezer is British slang for a man, especially an older one

explanation.surface: Someone eavesdrops on a grumpy old fellow who often vents his anger.
explanation.walkthrough: GEEZER is British slang for a bloke; the definition's 'lets off steam' reads as temper but means a spouting spring.
explanation.definitionFit: A geyser is a hot spring that periodically erupts with water and vapour.

clue.text: Possibly malevolent look one vile Yemeni adopts

indicators.note: adopts means takes in, so the words hold the answer within them

explanation.surface: A wicked man from Yemen takes on a menacing glare.
explanation.definitionFit: The evil eye is a glare believed in folklore to cause harm, so a look that may be malicious.

clue.text: Hard work, many discovered, to produce advertising jingle

parts.note: a slog is tiring hard work

indicators.note: discovered means uncovered, the word many stripped of its outer letters

explanation.surface: Many people found that a catchy advertising tune took real effort.
explanation.definitionFit: A slogan is a catchy phrase used in marketing, close in sense to a jingle.

clue.text: Stocking only occasionally goes over large leg

indicators.note: in a down clue goes over places the first piece above the rest
occasionally means every other letter of the word only

parts.note: on is the leg side in cricket

explanation.surface: A stocking only sometimes stretches over a big leg.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side of the field is also called the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylon stockings are commonly called by the fabric's name, often in the plural.

clue.text: Rock musicians led away to find air transport

indicators.note: away means the word led is taken off the band's name

parts.note: Led Zeppelin were a famous British rock band
taken as written

explanation.surface: A band's frontman steers the group off to catch a flight.
explanation.definitionFit: A zeppelin is a rigid airship, an early kind of aircraft.

clue.text: Acquires finally valuable area for expansion purposes

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A company eventually buys up prime land in order to grow.
explanation.definitionFit: To earn is to gain or get money or credit, so a synonym of acquires.

clue.text: Screen actress in minor role many condemned

indicators.note: condemned suggests the words are wrecked and remade in another order

explanation.surface: A film star cast in a small part that lots of people criticised.
explanation.definitionFit: Marilyn Monroe was a Hollywood film star of the 1950s.

clue.text: Wealth of old coins impressing university lecturer initially

indicators.note: impressing means pressing in, so the coins enclose the next letters

parts.note: pence are coins

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the word lecturer

explanation.surface: An academic is dazzled by a hoard of antique coins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'impressing' puts U plus L inside PENCE, giving PULENCE after O.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulence is great riches or luxury, a synonym of wealth.

clue.text: Attention surrounds setter regularly in certain time of year

indicators.note: surrounds says the attention word goes round the other letters

parts.note: giving an ear means paying attention

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of the word setter

explanation.surface: Someone listens closely as a crossword compiler keeps to a seasonal schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attention' is the ear one lends; 'surrounds' puts it round the odd letters picked by 'regularly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Easter is the spring festival, a particular season in the Christian calendar.
